observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x004adb04 MOV dword ptr [EBP-0x4],ECX stores the incoming ECX and 0x004adb07 reloads it, so the receiver arrives in ECX. There is no stack argument: the body never reads [EBP+8] and the terminating instruction 0x004adb10 is a bare RET with no immediate, so the callee pops nothing. Ghidra labels the decompilation __fastcall, which is its default for a one-ECX-input leaf and is contradicted by the absence of any stack read. The sibling setters in the same family (0x004ada80, 0x004adae0, 0x004adb20) all end in RET 0x4, which is the __thiscall form, and their matching getters (0x004adaa0, 0x004adb40) end in a bare RET exactly as this one does.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the 32-bit float stored at receiver+0x40, returned unchanged
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x004adb0a is FLD dword ptr [EAX+0x40], an 80-bit x87 load whose 32-bit single-precision source is promoted to extended precision; nothing is written to EAX, XMM0 or any general register after the load. Every inspected caller consumes the result with FSTP, either to memory (0x0043fda3, 0x005d37c7) or to [ESP+0xc] (0x005d37bc), which is only correct for an ST0 return. On x86-32 a float return therefore does NOT travel in XMM0 as it would under a different ABI, and Ghidra's float10 rendering is the accurate one.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX, spilled to [EBP-0x4] at 0x004adb04 and reloaded at 0x004adb07
observed_original_abi.frame: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / PUSH ECX, torn down by MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP. Four bytes of frame, holding nothing but the spilled receiver.

layout.x87_note: FLD pushes exactly one value onto the x87 stack and the epilogue contains no FFREE, so the function is stack-neutral for the FPU: exactly one push in, one value out.

observed_mechanics: 0x004adb04 MOV dword ptr [EBP-0x4],ECX followed by 0x004adb07 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP-0x4]: the receiver is spilled and immediately reloaded. The spill is redundant, which is why the same function compiled as MOV EAX,ECX / FLD [EAX+0x40] / RET elsewhere; it is a register-allocation artefact, not an invariant.
0x004adb0a FLD dword ptr [EAX + 0x40] is the entire semantic content: a 32-bit float load from field offset +0x40, promoted to x87 extended precision
0x004adb10 is C3, a bare RET with no immediate, which is what proves the callee pops zero stack words
The body contains no TEST, no CMP and no conditional branch of any kind: there is no null check on the receiver and no validation of any field

0x0043fda6 MOV ECX,[EBP-0x6c] / 0x0043fda9 CALL 0x004adb00 / 0x0043fdae PUSH ECX / 0x0043fdaf FSTP float ptr [ESP]: the caller reserves a stack slot, calls, then stores ST0 over the pre-pushed ECX. This is the canonical MSVC x86 idiom for passing a float by value and proves the ST0 return.

0x005d37b5..0x005d37d1 calls 0x004adaa0 (+0x38), 0x004adb00 (+0x40) and 0x004adb40 (+0x44) back to back on the SAME receiver EBX, storing the three results to [ESP+0xc], [ESI+0x2c] and [ESI+0x24] respectively. The three-field read as a group is the strongest available evidence about what the field means.

The same code region holds a matched setter for every field this getter family touches: 0x004ada80 stores a float to +0x38, 0x004adac0 to +0x3c, 0x004adae0 to +0x40, 0x004adb20 to +0x44, 0x004adba0 stores a byte to +0x4c, 0x004adbe0 to +0x4d and 0x004adb60 to +0x4e, each ending in RET 0x4

Every setter in that family uses MOVSS (SSE) while every getter uses FLD (x87), so the field is genuinely a float and the asymmetry is a codegen choice for the return path, not evidence of a different type

sdk_correspondence.basis: Twelve accessors disassembled in the 0x004ada80..0x004adbe0 range touch seven distinct offsets (+0x38, +0x3c, +0x40, +0x44, +0x4c, +0x4d, +0x4e), and Spore/Editors/EditorModel.h is the only SDK struct examined whose declared field order and types reproduce all seven: float mBounds at 0x38, float mFeetBounds at 0x3c, float mMinHeight at 0x40 with the documented default -2.0, float mMaxHeight at 0x44 with the documented default 2.0, bool mShowHiddenHandles at 0x4c, bool mShowBoneLengthHandles at 0x4d, bool mUseBoundsForDelete at 0x4e. The seven-offset agreement is recorded as SUPPORTED and the class is NOT claimed.

semantic_contract: A leaf, non-virtual, side-effect-free accessor on a model-state object. ECX receiver, no stack argument, bare RET, and a 32-bit float returned in x87 ST0 - not in XMM0 and not in EAX. The whole contract is: return the four bytes at receiver+0x40 interpreted as an IEEE-754 single, promoted to extended precision. There is no null check on the receiver, no validation of the field, no branch of any kind, and no memory written anywhere. The field is the middle element of a contiguous float run whose lower and upper neighbours are read by two sibling getters in the same code region, and all three are read together by at least one caller, so the field is a member of a low/high/radius triple rather than an isolated scalar.
classification_rationale: The behaviour is completely determined: a 17-byte, 9-instruction, branch-free leaf whose entire content is one FLD at a known offset, with the return register, the frame shape and the absence of callee cleanup all read directly from the listing. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because the owning type is bounded rather than established, and the bound is named: the twelve sibling accessors reproduce seven offsets of a single SDK struct declaration exactly, but no vtable for that class exists in the typed program and Ghidra's xref sweep over the SDK-recorded EditorModel::SetName returns only call references, so the class cannot be closed from the binary. Under the batch's own definition this is precisely the BOUNDED_SEMANTIC case, an owning type that is bounded rather than established. A STRONG_SEMANTIC claim would require either a located vtable or runtime evidence, and neither exists.
semantic_findings: The return travels in x87 ST0. Reconstructing this as a function returning float through XMM0 would be ABI-wrong on this target, so the reconstruction is written to return a C++ float and the ABI note records the ST0 path explicitly.

The receiver spill at 0x004adb04 followed immediately by a reload at 0x004adb07 is redundant; a sibling getter in the same region compiles the same operation without the frame. It is a register-allocation artefact and is preserved only as a structural note, not as an invariant.

The bare RET is what distinguishes this getter from its siblings the setters. The setters in the same family end in RET 0x4 because they take one stack argument; the getters end in a bare RET because they take none. Ghidra's __fastcall label on the decompilation is a default for a one-register-input leaf and is contradicted by the body.
The function dereferences the receiver exactly once with no test, so a null receiver faults. That precondition is preserved rather than defended.

The field at +0x40 sits in the middle of a float run +0x38/+0x3c/+0x40/+0x44 that ends where a run of one-byte fields begins at +0x4c. The type boundary is read directly from the sibling accessors' operand sizes, not inferred from the SDK.

The three-float read at 0x005d37b5..0x005d37d1 (same receiver, three consecutive getter calls, results stored to three different destinations) is the only observed evidence for the field's role, and it is consistent with a vertical extent bracket rather than a scalar preference.
The address is not in any vtable Ghidra has typed, and 11 real calls from 8 unrelated functions with no stack-argument setup is the expected shape for an inline-class accessor.
unresolved_questions: Which class owns the receiver. Seven offsets match Spore/Editors/EditorModel.h exactly and no other examined SDK struct does, but no vtable was located and this binary has no RTTI, so the class is recorded as a candidate and not claimed.
What the field at +0x40 is called. mMinHeight is the SDK candidate; the independent binary evidence is only that it is the middle of a three-float run read together.

Is +0x48 really a fourth float, i.e. mMinimumLeglessCreatureHeight? It is inferred from the type boundary at +0x4c and from the SDK ordering; no accessor for it was found in the disassembled range and no read or write of +0x48 was observed.

Where is the getter for +0x3c (mFeetBounds) and the getter for +0x4e? Only setters were found in 0x004ada80..0x004adbe0, so the accessor family is incomplete and the field survey is bounded by the range that was disassembled.
What are the nine uninspected call sites doing with the value, and does the one at 0x005b49be belong to a function Ghidra could not attribute?

Why do three of the eight resolved callers take the receiver from an outer object's vtable slot +0x28 rather than from a field? That indirection is observed at 0x00485ba5..0x00485bad but the outer object's class is not identified.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this function. Static analysis cannot show the live value of the +0x40 float, so the SDK's documented -2.0 default is unverified for the shipping build.
A trace with a concrete receiver is required before the owning class can be named, because no vtable could be located.

A differential test must confirm that the value is returned in ST0 and not in XMM0 in the shipping build. The static evidence for ST0 is strong - FLD with no FXCH and FSTP at every consumer - but it is static.
